terms.grammar: adjective, with mēnsis; also a masculine noun (sc. mēnsis)
terms.comment: Kalendae, Nōnae, Īdūs Aprīlēs: the 1st, 5th and 13th. Varro and Ovid derive the name from aperīre, the month that opens the earth (Varro, LL 6.33; Ov. F. 4.87–89); its real origin is uncertain.

phrases.latin: Magnum prōventum poētārum annus hic attulit: tōtō mēnse Aprīlī nūllus ferē diēs, quō nōn recitāret aliquis.
phrases.english: This year has brought a fine crop of poets: in the whole of April there was hardly a day when someone was not giving a reading.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 77.
